title: How Ruben Hassid trains Claude on his best LinkedIn posts to write new ones
summary: Ruben walks through scraping a profile's LinkedIn posts cheaply via Apify, having Claude analyze them into a report and SOP, then turning that into a reusable /skill that generates new posts from proven patterns. He also shows how to clone the recipe of a single viral post, and is candid about the limits: AI mirrors rather than creates, and only works if past posts were good.

principles.text: Train AI on your own best posts, not generic internet advice, so output reflects what actually worked for you.
principles.quote: And this is optimized only from MY best posts, nothing from the internet _(which is probably outdated anyway)._

principles.text: Never automate from your own LinkedIn account; extract public posts through a third-party tool instead.
principles.quote: It’s important not to do it from your account (_never do any automation_).

principles.text: Turn the analysis into a reusable skill so you stop re-pasting the same prompt and context.
principles.quote: You want to create a skill inside Claude to not copy & paste the same prompt and the same context, over and over again.

principles.text: Capture the recipe of a single ultra-viral post (format, hook, caption cadence) as a skill to repeat it.
principles.quote: Just create a Claude skill to capture the “recipe” of that post for any new post.

principles.text: Don't repeat one viral recipe endlessly; audiences tire of the same format.
principles.quote: It’s not because burgers are tasty that you want to eat burgers every day.

principles.text: AI is great at digesting context but not creative; pair it with your own human pattern-matching.
principles.quote: But it’s awesome when you can combine its capacity to digest a lot of context (like 400+ posts) + your human ability to do pattern-matching.
